intended_object: The universal property of the Grothendieck ring K(A) of a semiring A: for any ring S, restricting along the canonical map A → K(A) gives a bijection between ring homomorphisms K(A) → S and semiring homomorphisms A → S. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The forward map is `liftRingHom`, which extends a semiring homomorphism f : A →+* S to K(A) using the additive Grothendieck lift of f. The inverse is composition with `ofRingHom`, the canonical ring homomorphism A → K(A). The two inverse laws are proved from `liftRingHom_of` and from `ringHom_ext`, which says a ring homomorphism out of K(A) is determined by its values on generators. Together these give exactly the standard universal property of the ring completion of a semiring, i.e. it is left adjoint to the forgetful functor from rings to semirings.

The generality is the natural one. The source is any semiring, and the target is any ring, which it must be so that the additive lift exists. Commutativity is not assumed, and the source and target universes are independent.

Mathlib has `Algebra.GrothendieckAddGroup` only as an additive group (only `Mathlib/Algebra/AffineMonoid/Embedding.lean` refers to it in the version searched). It has no ring structure on it and no ring-level lift equivalence, so this equivalence has no Mathlib counterpart.
